newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher in active trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed higher for the seventh consecutive session in extremely active trading as brewing giant Bavaria continued to attract strong buying interest.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.65 percent at 17,149.32 on what brokers described as a near record volume of more than 22.5 billion pesos.
Bogota's IBB edged up a full percentage point, meanwhile, ending at 1,123.28 on well above-average volume of more than 19 billion pesos.

"There was demand from foreign funds and locals, speculation and cross-trades ... All these ingredients hadn't come together in a single day for a long time now," one Bogota-based trader said of the volatile trading session.

Bavaria, the country's most active stock, continued rising on its recent announcement of an imminent share split and what brokers described as persistent market rumors that a stake in the company might be sold to Brazilian brewer Brahma.
Bavaria president Augusto Lopez told Reuters he had no news of any offer from Brahma, however, and a spokeswoman for Brahma said no negotiations were underway with its Bavaria.
Bavaria closed up 3.84 percent in Medellin at a new all-time high of 8,300 pesos per share despite the denials.
Large cross-trades in companies affiliated with the Sindicato Antioqueno accounted for much of the day's trading volume.

The day's gainers included blue chip Banco Ganadero despite being downgraded to hold from buy by ING Barings in New York. The rating was cut following the solid performance of its common and preferred ADRs over the last year. Ganadero's preferred stock closed up 3.70 percent in Bogota at 280 pesos per share.
